summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Lighthouse Health through the Model Catalog UI, open-model selection, benchmark results, and the compatibility matrix for hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Customer asked about latency vs cost tradeoffs, quantization/accuracy regressions, and VPC/KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: share detailed benchmark CSVs, compatibility matrix deck, schedule a tech deep dive on private deployment and KMS integration, and provision a short pilot environment.
topics: Compatibility matrix: hosted vs dedicated vs private
transcript:
[00:00] Carlos: hey everyone thanks for joining. we can wait one more minute for emily to hop in but, um, we'll get started on time. this is carlos from redwood, ae on the account.
[00:18] Dr. Emily: sorry running a bit late, hi all.
[00:24] Carlos: no worries. quick round of intros?
[00:30] Marcus: Marcus here, head of ml at Lighthouse Health. we own the inference stack for patient triage.
[00:36] Sofia: Sofia, security eng, will be focused on compliance and data residency.
[00:40] Priya: hi i'm priya, solutions engineer at redwood, i'll be running the demo and the benchmarks part.
[00:46] Jordan: jordan on product, i'll cover catalog features and rollout controls.
[00:52] Carlos: ok great. agenda real quick: model catalog walkthrough, how to pick open models, show benchmarks and the compatibility matrix, and then q&a and next steps.
[01:10] Dr. Emily: sounds good. our main constraints: latency under 250ms p95 for short prompts, strict PHI handling (on-prem for certain flows) and cost targets.
[01:25] Carlos: perfect that's helpful. Marcus, can you say typical prompt lengths / tokens?
[01:30] Marcus: usually 16-80 tokens for triage prompts, occasional long context at 512 tokens for threads. qps target is around 15-25 during peak, but bursts up to 80.
[01:44] Priya: ok good, that maps to the catalog profiles we tuned for short seqs vs long seqs, i'll show the performance curves.
[01:52] Jordan: quick note on the catalog: each model has a performance profile (latency/cost per token), accuracy evals against our public eval sets, and compatibility flags for features like streaming, function calling, and kv cache.
[02:08] [02:08] Priya: jumping into the UI now, top left is model search. you can filter by architecture, open-source license, quantization support, and certified performance tiers. i'm selecting 'open models' and sorting by p95 latency for 32-token prompts.
[02:30] Priya: you can see the top hits: redwood-llama2-q8_32 (quantized), ggml-vicuna-1.3, and oss-flan-t5-opt. each card shows tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens approximated. note that the quantized variants trade a bit of accuracy for 2-3x lower cost.
[02:52] Marcus: when you say accuracy tradeoff, what's the metric? rouge or f1 on our tasks?
[02:58] Priya: good question. we surface model-level evals: exact match, rouge-L, and a small rw eval tied to our community datasets. for custom tasks you can upload eval sets; the catalog will run a quick comparative eval. the small accuracy loss for q8 quantization is typically 1-3% on LM benchmarks but highly model dependent.
[03:20] Sofia: when you run those evals where does the data go? we need assurances about data retention.
[03:26] Carlos: by default evals run in your project with ephemeral storage; we have a policy to not persist the eval inputs unless you opt in, and for private deployments all eval runs stay in customer VPC. we'll share the SOC2 and data-retention docs after the call.
[03:42] Dr. Emily: can you show a compatibility matrix? we need to know which models support streaming, kv cache, and function calling because our integration relies on streaming for realtime UX.
[03:54] Priya: sure — switching to the compatibility tab. you see a matrix with rows for model families and columns for features. e.g., some older opt variants don't support efficient kv-cache shipping so streaming + walkback is poorer. redwood-llama2-q8 supports streaming, function calling, and kv-cache in both hosted and dedicated. for private, it depends on the runtime image — our private bundle includes the same runtime kernels so parity is high.
[04:22] Marcus: ok parity is good. about private parity — are the kernels optimized differently on say A100 vs T4? we run mixed infra.
[04:31] Priya: yes we surface the chosen kernel set per hardware. the catalog will recommend model quantization and kernel selection per hardware profile. on T4 we recommend certain quantized variants for cost reasons, on A100 you can run fp16 with lower latency.
[04:44] [04:44] Jordan: and there's a hardware compatibility overlay — you can pick region and hw and see the expected p95 from our internal bench for that exact combination.
[04:53] Dr. Emily: can you show a benchmark example?
[04:57] Priya: pulling the benchmark viewer now. this is a redwood-run across three seq lengths 32/128/512, measured across gp2 (A100), gtx-t4 and cpu fallback. here's a CSV link with raw runs. note the p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:20] Marcus: i see the redwood-llama2-q8 row has 120ms p95 at 32 tokens on A100?
[05:26] Priya: yep that's from our internal runs. on T4 it's closer to 210ms. we also show error bars since runtime batching impacts tail latency.
[05:36] Marcus: what about accuracy comparisons to openai gpt-4o-mini? not exact parity but can you approximate?
[05:42] Priya: we provide benchmarked accuracy on shared eval sets; for tough instruction-following gpt-4 series still leads but certain open models with instruction tuning are within margin on domain-specific tasks. we can run your eval set and produce a side-by-side.
[05:55] Sofia: circling back to security, for private we need KMS integration and audit logs. can redwood integrate with our cloud kms and push all audit logs to our SIEM?
[06:05] Carlos: yes — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for private deployments. audit logs can be forwarded to CloudWatch/Stackdriver or to S3/Cloud Storage with retention policies. we'll attach the runbook.
[06:18] Sofia: and for hosted API, is there an option for customer-managed keys?
[06:22] Carlos: hosted currently uses redwood-managed keys but we offer a premium customer-managed keys option for enterprise plans; that's part of the Private or Dedicated offerings.
[06:32] Marcus: on cost — curious about batching and how it affects latency for p95. if we configure batching aggressively to save cost will we blow the latency SLO?
[06:41] Priya: there's a tradeoff. catalog profiles include batching recommendations per workload; we show a simulated p95 for different batch sizes. for bursty QPS you can use small batch windows and prefix KV caching to avoid re-generation which preserves latency. we also have smart routing to route low-cost traffic to cheaper variants.
[06:59] [06:59] Dr. Emily: can you demo model selection for our triage use-case? so we pick a model that fits 250ms p95 and under $X per 1k tokens.
[07:08] Priya: sure; using filter: p95 <= 250ms on T4, cost < $5 per 1k tokens (example). results: redwood-llama2-q8 and ggml-vicuna-1.3. clicking compare — it shows accuracy delta, and recommended quantization and estimated monthly cost at your target QPS.
[07:30] Marcus: the estimated monthly cost assumes certain batching; are those assumptions visible?
[07:34] Priya: yes click 'cost details' — we surface batch size, average tokens per request, and assumed utilization. you can tweak those to generate a new estimate.
[07:45] Marcus: good. i'd like the raw numbers so we can plug into our cost model.
[07:48] Priya: that's the benchmarks CSV I linked earlier; we'll send a cleaned version with the exact assumptions.
[07:55] Sofia: compliance question: do you isolate model fine-tuning artifacts? we may want to fine-tune on PHI inside our VPC — is that supported?
[08:05] Carlos: private deployment supports in-VPC fine-tune runs; artifacts remain in customer storage and never traverse redwood-managed buckets unless explicitly shared. for Dedicated we can provide isolation guarantees via tenant pools.
[08:19] Dr. Emily: what's typical time to provision a private instance? we're evaluating time-to-production for pilot in january.
[08:27] Jordan: for our packaged private bundle, typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for a standard config; if you need air-gapped or HSM integration add 1-2 weeks. we can fast-track pilots.
[08:38] Marcus: about model updates and rollback — how do you handle model versioning and can we pin to a model sha?
[08:46] Priya: yes every catalog entry links to a model artifact id and version. you can pin to sha and create rollout policies (canary, percentage-based, auto-rollback if quality regression detected by eval set).
[08:59] [08:59] Dr. Emily: nice. can i see an example of a rollout config?
[09:03] Priya: opening the rollouts demo; here's a canary where 10% traffic goes to new model for 24 hours, monitored by our quality hooks. if accuracy drops >2% on your eval set we auto-roll back and notify.
[09:16] Marcus: that automation is useful. how intrusive are quality checks? do you need to mirror production traffic?
[09:22] Priya: we recommend a sampled mirror for high-signal checks; the system supports synthetic tests too. mirroring affects cost but we offer sampled mirroring to minimize overhead.
[09:33] Sofia: for the audit trail — how granular are logs around inference input/outputs? we need to show who triggered a model rollout and link to the exact artifact used for each request for audits.
[09:45] Carlos: audit logs include model_artifact_id, deployment_id, user id of operator who triggered rollout, timestamps, and a link to the config diff. for PHI we recommend enabling redaction in-flight and storing only hashes unless you opt into storing payloads for debugging.
[09:59] Marcus: can you show the API example for model selection? we want to automate fallback to cheaper variants when latency is too high.
[10:07] Priya: sure — this is a sample call: POST /v1/infer with model: "redwood-llama2-q8" and the runtime policy header: route-preference: cost|latency ; if latency threshold passed we'll route to a faster variant or fall back to a model with larger capacity. the SDK also supports built-in fallback policies.
[10:29] Dr. Emily: in practice how often will the router swap models? do we get cold starts?
[10:34] Priya: router decisions are per-request and consider current load and KV cache hit; cold starts may happen when model variant isn't warm, but we keep a small pool of warm workers for low-latency services. you can also pin warm workers for critical endpoints in Dedicated.
[10:49] Marcus: i want to understand quantization regression risks — do you provide per-task delta so we can decide if q8 is acceptable?
[10:57] Priya: yes — when you run your eval set the report includes per-task deltas between float16 and q8 and confidence intervals. we'll run your triage eval and call out any edge-cases.
[11:12] [11:12] Dr. Emily: hypothetical: if we see a regression on a safety-critical prompt, is there an automated fallback to float16 or to a hosted safer model?
[11:21] Priya: yes, you can configure automatic fallback policies where safety-critical routes hit a more conservative model or are routed only to Dedicated/Private float16 instances. the rule engine is declarative.
[11:34] Sofia: can you provide the SOC2 artifact and encryption whitepaper?
[11:38] Carlos: absolutely, will share SOC2 report and the KMS integration doc after this call.
[11:45] Marcus: ok next, benchmarks methodology — is your reported p95 measured over sustained qps or microbench burst tests?
[11:53] Priya: both. we run microbench to capture minimal tail behavior and sustained tests to capture batching and queuing effects. CSV includes test type column.
[12:03] Marcus: will you run a mirror of our traffic shape for the pilot?
[12:07] Priya: yes that's part of the SE pilot work — we'll run a workload-matched benchmark in our staging using either synthetic shape or a small redacted sample you provide.
[12:16] Dr. Emily: timeline for pilot?
[12:18] Carlos: propose pilot start week of Jan 4th, duration two weeks, objective: validate p95 < 250ms for triage endpoints and cost < target.
[12:28] Sofia: is there an NDA we need before sending sample data?
[12:31] Carlos: we have an NDA template; we can exchange that today. for PHI you should only send redacted samples until NDA and private project are provisioned.
[12:43] Marcus: one last technical — kv cache behavior across variants: if we route to a different quantized variant does kv cache invalidate?
[12:52] Priya: KV cache formats are compatible across our model variants within the same family; some cross-family switches require cache warm-up. the catalog will warn if switching invalidates cache.
[13:04] [13:04] Jordan: moving toward wrap-up. to recap redwood will send the model catalog deck, the compatibility matrix PDF, and benchmark CSV. SE will run the custom triage eval and two latency tests on mirrored shape. sales will propose pilot dates and pricing sketch.
[13:20] Dr. Emily: thanks, useful. a few people on our side will review the SOC2/KMS docs and follow up with specific compliance questions.
[13:29] Carlos: great. any other questions?
[13:33] Marcus: none atm.
[13:35] Sofia: no.
[13:36] Priya: ok we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the tech deep dive.
[13:41] Carlos: thanks everyone, we'll send notes and next steps.
[13:45] Dr. Emily: thanks all, bye.

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-hearings in system capturings (e.g., "K-V cash" appears in some auto captions), speaker alignment was checked lightly. Timestamps approximate every 30-90 seconds.
